solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Helicopter ejecting hotel inspector, for example

indicators.note: ejecting means throwing out, so the hotel letter is removed from the aircraft's slang name

parts.note: chopper is the informal name for a helicopter
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a helicopter, perhaps a police inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from CHOPPER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police inspector is one example of a policeman, slangily called a copper in Britain.

clue.text: Unusual round after start

indicators.note: after puts the round piece following the start piece

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
a beat is a policeman's regular round

explanation.surface: Something odd after a round has just begun.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: A bit of flower power — and other things

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Flower power from the hippie era, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower power' looks like one phrase, the hippie slogan, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf forming the head of a bloom is one of these.

clue.text: Short tea breaks initially satisfied current controllers

indicators.note: breaks means shatters, so the letters of short tea are broken up and rearranged
initially means the first letter of satisfied

explanation.surface: Brief tea breaks satisfied people at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short tea breaks' reads as brief pauses for tea, but 'Short' is fodder, not a shortening signal; 'breaks' rearranges it with 'tea' into RHEOSTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheostats are variable resistors used to regulate electric current.

clue.text: Restricted dealing in trade covering source of oil

indicators.note: covering means the anagram wraps round the next piece
dealing, as in dealing cards, mixes up the letters of the words in trade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here taken from oil

explanation.surface: Commerce in oil was restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing in trade' reads as commerce, but 'in' is fodder; 'dealing' makes RATINED and 'covering' wraps it round the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are rationed are restricted to a fixed allowance per person.

clue.text: Declines employment opportunities ultimately given to football official

parts.note: the ref, referee, officiates at football
use is the employment of something

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of opportunities

explanation.surface: A referee turns down job openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employment opportunities' reads as job openings but splits into USE and the S at the end of 'opportunities'.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuses and declines are synonyms, meaning turns down.

clue.text: Tourist attraction with time for son to get drunk

indicators.note: with time for means time replaces son, one letter swapped for another

parts.note: a sight is something tourists go to see

explanation.surface: A tourist spot where a son gets drunk given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for intoxicated.

clue.text: People rowing creating chaos in a newsroom

indicators.note: creating chaos signals that the letters of a newsroom are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Rowers wreak havoc in a newspaper office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' suggests arguing, which suits the newsroom, but means sculling.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarswomen are female rowers.

clue.text: Facilities in empty European train?

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, leaving only the outer letters of European

parts.note: a suite is a train of attendants, a retinue

explanation.surface: Toilets on a European train with nobody aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: En suite rooms have their own bathroom attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a private bathroom attached to a bedroom, so facilities in a coy sense.

clue.text: Symbols of authority priest understands

parts.note: a Catholic priest is addressed as Father
figures, as in 'that figures', means works out or understands

explanation.surface: A priest grasps what the symbols of authority mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: people looked up to as protective and authoritative are called this.

clue.text: Practical people mostly relax welcoming top celebs

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so one piece goes inside the other
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rest is to relax
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Down-to-earth people mostly relax when receiving famous guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-list is a showbiz term for the most sought-after celebrities; 'mostly' leaves RES and 'welcoming' takes the list in.
explanation.definitionFit: Realists are pragmatic people who deal with things as they actually are.

clue.text: City dweller getting personal in match

indicators.note: in places the personal piece inside the match

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
own means belonging to oneself, personal

explanation.surface: A city resident gets personal during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: Townie is informal for someone living in a town or city rather than the country.

clue.text: A power unit rejected by old capital city

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters of a power unit are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: A capital city where power has been turned down by the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A WATT into TTAWA, which follows O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

clue.text: Not in favour of new form of literature

parts.note: anti means opposed to, not in favour of
novel means new

explanation.surface: Opposed to a new kind of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel is fiction that deliberately rejects conventional novel structure.

clue.text: Good man! Steak and French tart

parts.note: ST, saint, is a crossword stand-in for a good man
rump is a cut of steak
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An exclamation of praise followed by a menu: steak and a French tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' is not the pastry but the old insult for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned word for a prostitute or loose woman, as is tart.

clue.text: Considering revision of grade during call

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the call

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters of grade are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thinking about changing a grade while on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' is a telephone call in the British sense of ringing; 'revision of' makes EGARD and 'during' sets it in the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarding means concerning or with respect to, as does considering.

clue.text: Militant craftsman confronted by pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: An aggressive craftsman is put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronted by' puts P in front of ARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a militant fighter or an aggressively committed supporter.

clue.text: Help for a newsreader reporting traffic jam?

indicators.note: reporting suggests telling aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase for a traffic jam

parts.note: a traffic jam is a queue of cars, so an auto queue

explanation.surface: Something a newsreader uses while reading the traffic news.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTO (car) plus QUEUE (line) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen showing the script to a newsreader, a teleprompter.

clue.text: Token oilman working after a touch of nerves

indicators.note: a touch of means just a little, the first letter of nerves
working means in operation, signalling the letters of oilman are reworked

explanation.surface: An oil worker on the job after a bit of nervousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Token' is an adjective here, as in a token gesture; 'working' makes OMINAL, which goes 'after' the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal payment is a token one, in name only.

clue.text: Energy retained in using oddly natural talent

indicators.note: retained in means held inside, so the energy letter goes inside the anagram
oddly means in an odd way, signalling a rearrangement of using

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy kept in reserve by using one's natural gift in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns USING into GNIUS, with E 'retained in' after the G. 'oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but that gives nothing useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius is exceptional natural ability or talent.

clue.text: Experience reporting to work

parts.note: someone who reports to a boss works under them
go means work, function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: The experience of reporting for work.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it.

clue.text: Gems thrown out by last one standing

indicators.note: thrown out by means given off by these words, so the answer is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Jewels hurled by the final survivor in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'laST ONE Standing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones is the jeweller's word for gems, precious stones.

clue.text: Only about five work out

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for only surrounds the numeral

parts.note: sole means only, single
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Just about five minutes of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to work it out.

clue.text: Fishwives? Maybe!

parts.note: read the compound literally: wives who are part fish, the half-women of sea legend

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek query about women who sell fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A fishwife is a woman who sells fish, and by extension a loud coarse woman; here the word is taken as a wife who is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary sea maidens with a fish's tail could whimsically be called fish wives.

clue.text: Expert said sexpot needs to get rid of regulars

indicators.note: dropping the regularly spaced letters keeps only the alternate ones of said sexpot

explanation.surface: A specialist says a sex symbol must shed her usual admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S, I, S, X, O leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a highly skilled person, an expert.

clue.text: Polite and direct person such as Brunel?

parts.note: civil means courteous, polite
to engineer something is to bring it about, direct it

explanation.surface: A courteous, straightforward man like the Victorian engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian British builder of bridges, railways and ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel built bridges, tunnels and railways, the work of this profession.

clue.text: Fine source of water, I say

parts.note: well means in good health, fine
a well is a source of water dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A good spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are exclamations of mild surprise.

clue.text: Understand boy is making progress

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Grasp that the lad is coming along nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: someone who advances or succeeds in life is said to do this.
